title: Southern Fried Chicken
summary: Bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks are dry-brined, double-dredged and fried in a heavy pan for a thick, craggy, deeply seasoned crust.
equipment: large heavy cast-iron or deep frying pan (28-30 cm) or heavy pot
wire rack set over a tray

ingredients.item: chicken pieces on the bone: thighs and drumsticks, skin on
fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt
neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)

steps.title: Season and dry-brine
steps.text: Rub the chicken pieces all over with salt, garlic powder and paprika, then leave them uncovered in the fridge for at least 2 hours, or ideally overnight. This seasons the meat deep inside rather than just on the surface. It also dries the skin slightly, which helps the coating stick and crisp later.

steps.title: Mix flour and egg wash
steps.text: Whisk together the seasoned flour ingredients in one bowl, and beat the eggs with the milk in another. Having both stations ready before you start coating keeps the process quick and your hands cleaner.

steps.title: Dredge in stages
steps.text: Coat each piece first in flour, then dip into the egg wash, then back into the flour, pressing firmly so it clings in a thick, even layer. Rest the coated pieces on a rack for 15 minutes before frying. This resting time lets the flour hydrate and bind to the surface, so the crust holds together in hot oil instead of flaking off.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Pour oil into a heavy pot or deep cast-iron pan to a depth of 4-5 cm and heat to 175°C, checking with a frying thermometer. A heavy pan holds its heat steadily once the chicken goes in, which matters more here than the exact starting number.

steps.title: Fry in batches
steps.text: Fry 4 pieces at a time, starting with the dark meat, with the lid off. Expect the oil to drop to 150-160°C once the chicken is added; turn the pieces every 3-4 minutes and fry for 13-16 minutes in total. The steadier, slightly lower temperature after the drop lets the thick coating and bone-in meat cook through together without the crust burning first.

steps.title: Check doneness and drain
steps.text: Fry until the crust is deep golden brown and a thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 77-80°C. Lift onto a wire rack over a tray to drain, keeping cooked pieces in a 100°C oven while you fry the rest. Dark meat is safe from 74°C, but taking it a little higher melts more connective tissue, leaving the meat noticeably more tender.

steps.title: Season and serve
steps.text: Sprinkle the pieces lightly with salt as soon as they come off the rack. Salting while the crust is still hot and slightly oily helps it stick evenly rather than sliding straight off.

tips: Keep an eye on the oil temperature throughout frying - if it drops too low the coating turns pale and greasy instead of crisp, so adjust the heat as you go.
Don't skip the 15-minute rest after coating; frying straight away means the flour hasn't bonded to the chicken and much of it falls off in the oil.
Fry in small batches rather than crowding the pan, since too much chicken at once cools the oil too fast.
A frying thermometer is worth using rather than guessing - it's the easiest way to keep the crust golden rather than burnt or soggy.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Cool leftover fried chicken quickly and keep in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in a hot oven rather than the microwave to keep the crust crisp, until piping hot and 74°C in the centre. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
